full_judgment:
"Whether the Taxes Appellate Tribunal is justified in holding that the appeals are time barred counting the period of limitation of 60 days from 15.1.86, when the order of the Appellate Joint Commissioner was served on the Deputy Commissioner of taxes, inasmuch as under section 33(2) of the Income-Tax Act and section 158(4) of Ordinance XXXVI of 1984 the Commissioner of Taxes is entitled to file an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal within 60 days from the communication of order to him (Commissioner of Taxes)." 

 2. The aforesaid question arises out of the order of the Tribunal passed on April 26, 1987 in ITA No. 2131 of 1985-86 rejecting the appeal of the revenue on the ground of limitation. Therefore, we shall confine ourselves on the question of limitation. 

 4. Against the aforesaid order of the Joint Appellate Commissioner of Taxes the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes, Contractors, Circle-Il, Dhaka preferred the aforesaid appeal before the Taxes Appellate Tribunal, Bangladesh, Dhaka Division, Bench. The Tribunal by its order dated April 26, 1987 rejected the appeal on the ground of limitation holding that as the order of the AJCT was communicated to the DCT on 15.1.86 the appeal was to be filed by 18.3.86 and the appeal having been filed on 5.4.86 was time-barred. The Tribunal further held that the last date for filing the appeal on 4.4.1986 as stated in the Memorandum of the OCT was not correct and in absence of any application for condonation of delay the delay in filing the appeal could not be condoned. 

 5. On reference to the Order of the Tribunal we are of the opinion that the question as formulated referred to above arises out of the Order of the Tribunal. Under section 158 of the Income-Tax Ordinance, 1984 appeal lies to the Appellate Tribunal from an order passed under s. 128 or under section 156 by the Appellate Joint Commissioner of, Taxes and from the order of Inspecting Joint Commissioner exercising the powers of a Deputy Commissioner of Taxes under section 10 or from the order of Inspecting Joint Commissioner under section 120 of the Ordinance. Under sub-section (3) of s. 158 the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes may appeal 10 the Appellate Tribunal against the order of Appellate Joint Commissioner if the Commissioner directs him to prefer appeal against the order of the AJCT. Sub-section (5) of s. 156 enjoins the Appellate Joint Commissioner to communicate the order passed by him to the appellant, the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes and the Commissioner. Sub-section (4) of section 158 enjoins that every appeal under sub-section (1) or sub-section (3) shall be filed within 60 days of the date on which the order sought 10 be appealed against is communicated to the assessee or to the Commissioner, as the case may be Proviso to sub-section (4) authorises Appellate Tribunal to admit a time-barred appeal if it is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for not presenting the appeal within the period prescribed in sub-section (4) of section 158 of the Ordinance. Our reading of sub-section (3) of section 158 read with sub-section (5) of section 156 of the Ordinance is that the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes is not entitled to prefer an appeal against the order of the Appellate Joint Commissioner unless he is directed to me the appeal by the Commissioner of Taxes to whom the Appellate Joint Commissioner is bound to communicate its order on appeal. In this case it appears that the Appellate Tribunal took the view that as the order of the Appellate Joint Commissioner of Taxes was communicated to the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes on 15.1.86 the appeal filed before the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal on 5.4.86 was barred by Limitation. Mere communication of the order passed by the AJCT to the OCT is not enough. The order is also to be communicated to the Commissioner under sub-section (5) of s. 156 which is mandatory. Therefore, the expression "is communicated to the assessee or to the Commissioner," in our opinion, means communication by the AJCT of its order and not by the DCT. Thus, our reading of section 158(4) is that time runs for filing appeal before the Taxes Appellate Tribunal not from the date of communication of the order of AJCT to the OCT as has been held by the Tribunal but from date of communication of the order of AJC to the Commissioner. 

 6. From the statement made in paragraph 4 of this reference application it appears that the order of the Tribunal was communicated to the Commissioner on 4.2.86. Mr. Maksudur Rahman relying upon S. 12 of the Limitation Act contends that the day on which the order was communicated shall be excluded in reckoning the period of limitation. He submits that as the order of the Appellate Joint Commissioner was communicated on 4.2.86 the appeal filed on 5.4.86 was within time in view of the provision of s.12 of the Limitation Act and the Tribunal was not justified in holding that the appeal was barred by limitation. Mr. Maksudur Rahman further contends that as the appeal was filed within time the question of ruing an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act does not arise and the Tribunal was wrong in holding that there being no application for condonation of delay the delay could not be condoned. We find force in this contention of the Revenue. As we arc of the opinion that the Taxes Appellate Tribunal was not justified in rejecting the appeal on the ground of limitation we answer the question in the negative.
